sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the hatred that descended upon the nations of the world at Sinai parallels G-d's free choice to love Yaakov and hate Esav, rooted in Atzmus, and that the same dynamic applies to the hatred for the evil inclination, enabling the refinement of the animal soul through the revelation of the power of Atzmus.

translations.translation: A)
And it can be said,
that this is also the connection of "on this day" with
(the wilderness of)
Sinai,
that hatred descended upon the nations of the world who did not accept the Torah at that time.
For just as
Israel received the Torah because the Holy One, blessed be He, coerced them like a mountain suspended over them,
[this was] the revelation of love for Israel,
— "And He loves Yaakov,"
so too regarding the nations of the world who did not accept the Torah, this is because hatred descended upon the nations of the world — "And Esav I hated."
And this that "He loves Yaakov and Esav I hated" is not because of the virtue of Israel,
for the very fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, offered it
(the Torah)
to every nation and tongue
proves that the giving of the Torah is from the most exalted place,
where all virtues,
including even the virtue of "You are children to Hashem your G-d,"
have no standing there,
and both
(Israel and the nations of the world)
are equal — "Is not Esav a brother to Yaakov?"
Rather, in His free choice He chose to be "And He loves Yaakov and Esav I hated."
And this is the connection of "on this day" with the wilderness of Sinai,
that this hatred that descended upon the nations of the world is because He so chose in His free choice
(as above),
and the true essence of the concept of choice is only in Atzmus,
this.
And likewise regarding the matter of Sinai, that hatred descended upon the evil inclination
(within Israel),
through which the power was given to refine the emotions of the animal soul,
which is through the revelation of the power of Atzmus.
For that the G-dly soul is nullified to G-dliness,
including that even its extension
(love)
is in a state of nullification,
is not so novel,
and the main matter of the revelation of the power of Atzmus,
"on this day,"
is in this, that they came to the wilderness of Sinai,
the refinement and purification of the body and the animal soul.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies that while the main explanation in Torah Or focuses on the nullification of the "wilderness" aspect, the arousal and drawing down of the giving of the Torah (the drawing of Atzmus) comes specifically through the nullification that stems from the essence of the soul, which reaches Atzmus.

translations.translation: However, even so, the main explanation
(at length and in detail)
in the discourse in Torah Or regarding the virtue of Rosh Chodesh Sivan is about the matter of the nullification of the aspect of wilderness,
for the virtue in this, that even the existence is nullified
[the refinement of the emotions of the animal soul,
and likewise that the existence
(love)
of the G-dly soul is in nullification]
is that through this the power of Atzmus is revealed
(as above),
but in order to arouse and draw down the matter of the giving of the Torah
(the drawing of Atzmus)
it is through the nullification that comes from the essence of the soul,
for this nullification reaches Atzmus.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the unity of Israel on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, being "as one man with one heart," to the revelation of the root of the soul above the soul clothed in the body, which reaches Atzmus and arouses G-d's will to give them His Torah.

translations.translation: And one can connect this with that on Rosh Chodesh Sivan all of Israel were as one man with one heart,
and the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "Behold, the hour has come that I will give them My Torah,"
for this that they were as one man with one heart is through the revelation of the root of the soul that is above the soul clothed in the body,
and as explained in Tanya,
that all of Israel are truly brothers,
(specifically)
from the aspect of the root of their souls,
and therefore this that they were as one man
reached Atzmus and aroused in Him, so to speak, the will to give them His Torah.
